title: Why You Believe Information If It Is Repeated Often
hook: Why do you tend to believe repeated information?

narration.text: Your brain often mistakes familiarity for truth, even if the information is false.
The more you hear something, the easier it becomes for your mind to process.
This ease of processing feels like a signal that the information is correct.
This psychological quirk is called the illusory truth effect.
It means propaganda and advertising become more effective with repetition.
Be aware of this bias when you consume news and social media.
Comment if this surprised you, like the video, and subscribe for more insights into your mind.

description: Discover why repeated information, even if untrue, can start to feel like fact. Learn about the illusory truth effect and how it influences your beliefs every day. Understanding this cognitive bias can help you be more critical of the information you encounter.
topic: Why you tend to believe information more if it is repeated often, even if it is not true. This is called the 'illusory truth effect'.
